correctness.rationale: For the finite set \(W=F\cup(F-F\setminus\{0\})\), a unit vector \(u\) avoiding the finitely many directions in \(W\) gives a strict cosine bound \(c<1\). Choosing \(a\in(\max\{c,(1+\eta)^{-1}\},1)\) makes \(p(z)=\max\{\|z\|_2,|\langle u,z\rangle|/a\}\) agree exactly with the Euclidean norm on every required point and difference. Cauchy--Schwarz gives the global \(1+\eta\) comparison. The truncated Euclidean ball has positive-dimensional exposed faces, so the new norm is not strictly convex and therefore cannot be linearly isometric to Euclidean space. No finite experiment is used.

value.rationale: The result identifies a natural information-theoretic boundary of a new global rigidity theorem. It shows that the full sphere is essential in a strong exact sense: no finite metric sample works, even when every sampled point remains on the unit sphere, every sampled distance is preserved exactly, and the competing norm is arbitrarily close to Euclidean. The explicit perturbation also explains geometrically how rigidity can fail: unseen directions can be truncated to create flat faces without changing the sampled directions.
